This petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondent No.1 to 3 under Sec.166 of M.V.Act 1994 for the relief of compensation.

2. The brief facts of the case is as under; That on 11.06.2022 at about 6.15 p.m. Reddy Prasad was traveling as a pillion rider on Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-W-8766 being ridden by his friend Suresh near Seenappa's rock, on Yalagondahalli - Minanjenahalli Road, near Minjenahalli, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, the rider of the said motor cycle has ridden the same at high speed in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the road side SCCH 5 rock, due to the impact, Reddy Prasad has sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
3.
Prior to the accident, deceased Reddy Prasad was hale and healthy, aged about 26 years, working as Mason, thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, petitioners are put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of said motor cycle by its rider and Mulabagal Rural Police have registered a case in crime Ramya C.M vs Amaresh P.V on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122215259/
2 No.129/2022.

sentences.text: The 1st Respondent being the R.C.Owner, 2nd respondent being policy holder and 3rd respondent being insurer of the offending motor cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- to the petitioners with interest at the rate of 12% p.a. SCCH 5 4.
In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1/R.C.owner and respondent NO.2 being the insurance policy holder have remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.3/insurer has appeared before the tribunal through counsel and filed written statement by denying entire averments of the petition.

Ft admitted issuance of insurance policy to motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-08-W-8766 and liability to indemnify is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
There is no compliance of Sec.134(c) and Sec.158(6) of M.V.Act.
Respondent No.3 is entitled to take shelter under Sec.170 of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that, rider of the offending motor cycle did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

Further submitted that,
jurisdictional police have filed charge sheet under Sec.180, 181 of M.V.Act stating that rider of the said motor cycle was not holding valid driving licence as on SCCH 5 the date of accident, thereby owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
Further denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
Compensation claimed by the petitioner is on higher side.

5. On going through the rival pleadings of the parties, this tribunal has framed the following:
::ISSUES::
1. Whether the petitioners prove that, deceased Reddy Prasad died in the motor vehicle accident that occurred on 11.06.2022 at about 6.15 p.m. when deceased was travelling on a Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-08-W-8766 as a pillion rider near Seenappa's rock, Yalagondahalli - Minajenahalli Road, near Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District, at that time, the rider of the said motor cycle in a rash and negligent manner lost balance over his vehicle and dashed against a road side rock and caused accident, as mentioned in claim petition?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
SCCH 5 3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove their case, petitioner No.4 /mother of the deceased has deposed her evidence as PW-1 and marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.
on the other hand, Assistant Manager of respondent No.3 is examined as RW-1 and marked one document as per Ex.R.1 and closed his evidence.
7. Heard the arguments and perused the evidence available on record.

Then my findings on the above issues are as follows:

sentences.text: Issue No.1:-
The petitioners inorder to prove their case, petitioner No.4/mother of the deceased is SCCH 5 examined as PW-1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated petition averments.

Though she has been elaborately cross-examined by the Respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the evidence of the PW-1.
9.

Apart from the oral evidence, the PW-1 has got marked copy of FIR marked as Ex.P.1, copy of complaint marked as Ex.P.2, copy of spot mahazar with sketch is marked as Ex.P.3, copy of IMV Report is marked as Ex.P.4, copy of inquest is marked as Ex.P.5, copy of P.M.Report is marked as Ex.P.6 and copy of charge sheet is marked as Ex.P.7.
10.
On the other hand, Assistant Manager of respondent No. is examined as RW-1 and marked copy of policy as Ex.R.1.
Further except oral evidence, respondent No. has not taken any endeavors to disprove the petitioner's case about non-causing of the accident as SCCH 5 alleged in the petition and evidence of PW-1.

Since in the absence of iota of evidence, I have no hesitation to believe the case of the petitioners about death of deceased Reddy Prasad out of the accident held on 11.06.2022 when he was proceeding as pillion rider on Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-W-8766 near Seenappa's rock, on Yalagondahalli - Minajenahalli Road, near Minajenahalli, Mulabagal Taluk, Kolar District.
In the absence of iota of evidence, the arguments advanced by the petitioner's counsel are helpful to the case of the petitioner.
11. On the other hand, the police papers speaks that, very accident is occurred due to negligency of the rider of the Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 08-W-8766.

Under such circumstances, considering the said evidence and believing the evidence of the PW-1, this tribunal comes to the conclusion that, petitioners have SCCH 5 proved the above issue No.1 in their favour.
Accordingly I have answered above Issue No.1 in the affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- As per the case of the petitioners, deceased/Reddy Prasad was aged about 26 years as on the date of accident, for proof of age of the deceased, petitioners have produced copy of aadhar card marked as Ex.P.8, wherein date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1996, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.06.2022.

Accordingly relying on copy of aadhar card of the deceased,
age of the deceased is considered about 27 years as on the date of accident, hence multiplier 17 is applicable with reference to decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Varma and Others V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and others.

To prove the said facts, they have furnished notarized copy of aadhar cards of petitioner No.1 to 4 along with aadhar card of the deceased are marked as Ex.P.8 it reveals that, they are legal representatives of the deceased Reddy Prasad 15.

As per the case of Sarla Varma, if the number of dependents are 4 to 6, then 1/4th of the income is to SCCH 5 be deducted towards personal and living expenses of the deceased, so that, 1/4th of the income will be deducted at the time of calculation of compensation amount.

16. In the Special Leave Petition (CIVIL) No.25590 of 2014 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd.,
V/s. Pranay Sethi, The Hon'ble Apex Court has made it clear that, an addition of 40% to be added to the monthly income, if the deceased was aged below 40 years, in case of self employed person or person having fixed salary as future prospects.

future prospects (iii) 1/4th of (ii) of the Rs.20,650/- (-) same to be deducted Rs.5,162/- = towards personal and living expenses Monthly income Rs.15,488/-
(iv) Compensation after Rs.15,488/- x Rs.31,59,552/-
multiplier of 17 is 12 x 17 applied 18.

Petitioner No.2 and 3 being minor children of the deceased are entitled for Rs.20,000/-

5 each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioner No.4 being mother of the deceased is entitled for Rs.20,000/- towards filial consortium.

Accordingly I hold that, the Petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.32,69,552/-
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
SCCH 5 21.

Further during the course of arguments, respondent No.3 counsel Sri.KP vehemently argued that, there is no driving licence to the rider of the offending vehicle and charge sheet has been filed against the said rider and owner and both of them are liable to pay compensation and Insurance Company is not at all liable and there is no pay and recovery principle attracts to this case and admittedly accident was caused after amendment to the M.V.Act i.e., 01.04.2022.
22.

Further the respondent No.3 counsel has filed memo with rulings reported in MFA No.6154/2019 (MV- D) in between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., and MFA No.3297/2019 (MV-D) in between Adilakshmamma and others V/s. Raju B. and another.

sentences.text: So as per the rations laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the aforesaid rulings, the burden lies on the respondent No.2 who being the owner of the vehicle to pay compensation as alleged in the petition.

Ramya C.M vs Amaresh P.V on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122215259/
6 23.

Per contra, petitioner counsel resisted the said arguments and argued that, as per the evidence of PW-1 and petition averments, admittedly there is no driving licence to the offending vehicle rider for the date of the accident.
Further admittedly alleged accident was held on 11.06.2022 i.e., after amendment as well as came into SCCH 5 force new M.V.Act.
As stated supra, the principles of pay and recovery does not arise in this case.
Accordingly I am of the opinion that, respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay compensation, because he is the owner of the offending vehicle.

24. In the case on hand, respondent No.3 being the insurer has issued insurance policy bearing No.3361/02151047/000/00 which is valid for the period from 29.08.2021 to 28.08.2022 in respect of Bajaj Pulsar motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-08-W-8766, the alleged accident was occurred on 11.06.2022 it reveals that, as on the date of accident, insurance policy was in force.
As discussed above, respondent No.2 being the owner is alone liable to pay compensation with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. within 60 days from the date of this order.
With these views, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
SCCH 5 25. Issue No.3

: In view of the above reasoning and discussions to the above Issues No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
::ORDER

: : 
The claim petition filed by the Petitioners under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,69,552/- (Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Sixty Nine Thousand Five Hundred Fifty Two Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
The Respondent No.2 being the owner is alone shall deposit award amount with interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
The Petitioners are entitled for compensation at the ratio 60:10:10:20 in the award amount.

The petitioners No.1 and 4 are entitled to get release 60% of the award amount through e-payment directly to their accounts on furnishing the Bank A/c details and remaining 40% shall be SCCH 5 kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in their respective names.

Since Petitioner No.2 and 3 are minors, on deposit of the award amount, entire share shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any of the Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority with a liberty to draw accrued interest in the name of minor Petitioner guardian on the said fixed deposit once in 3 months for the benefit of minor Petitioners.
The Advocate Fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
